evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: We run monthly immunization camps in 36 villages of Udaipur district, Rajasthan. Behavior: mothers of children under two in Kherwara block bring the child to the camp on camp day each month. Field interviews confirmed the barrier is information: most mothers did not know the camp date or that the camp had moved to the anganwadi center; they said they would have come had they known. Mothers are home most mornings, about half of households have a phone held by the husband, the ASHA visits each hamlet roughly monthly, and the sarpanch announces things at the panchayat meeting that few women attend. Messengers we could field: the ASHA (our default), the anganwadi worker, the sarpanch, a mother who vaccinated on time, people the village names, and an SMS from the block office. None of them controls anything mothers need. We cover enough villages to split them. Who should deliver the camp-date message?
evals.expected_output: A choice of messenger in the output template that puts reach first because the barrier is that mothers have not heard the date.
assertions: Classifies the barrier as not heard and applies the reach-first rule.
The candidate table includes the ASHA as current sender and a person the village names.
Marks ratings not backed by what mothers said "assumed", and gives the reach question and the trust question, with who is asked.
Sets a comparison between villages with the chosen messenger and villages with the ASHA, with the camp register as outcome.
Does not write the message text and promises no effect size.
Ends with two or three next moves, each with its reason, and questions the user could ask next, with no single instruction.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: Who should send our savings messages?
evals.expected_output: The skill asks for the behavior and barrier, the audience, and the messengers the program could field, and produces nothing else.
assertions: Asks for the behavior and the confirmed barrier the message addresses.
Asks who the audience is and who talks to them about saving now.
Asks which messengers the program could field and whether any has power over the audience.
Does not recommend a messenger.
Does not fill the candidate table.
Says why it needs these answers.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: We're a payroll-linked savings program for workers at three garment and food-processing factories in peri-urban Kampala. Behavior: enrolled workers keep a monthly deduction into a savings account for six months. Interviews confirmed a trust barrier: workers doubt the money will be there when they want it, because a previous scheme at one factory collapsed. The factory owners are keen and want to deliver the message themselves at the Monday line meeting; they say the workers trust them. Other options are our field officer, a worker who has saved for a year already, and a line supervisor. Pick the messenger.
evals.expected_output: The skill produces the messenger choice, does not choose the factory owner, and names a safeguarding lead for any owner-delivered message.
assertions: Says the factory owner controls workers' wages and jobs.
Says workers may agree without believing, or feel unable to refuse.
Chooses a messenger other than the owner, or marks the owner as not to be used without review.
Treats the owners' statement that workers trust them as "assumed".
Names a safeguarding lead as the specialist and says what to bring.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: At our four rural clinics in Malawi, pregnant women stop taking iron-folate tablets after a few weeks. We think it's about what other people around them expect. Whose opinion actually counts for these women when they decide whether to keep taking the tablets? Their husbands? Mothers-in-law? The church?
evals.expected_output: The skill says the question is whose approval the women track, not who should deliver a message, and points to the skill for that.
assertions: Says this is a question about whose behavior or approval the women track.
Names map-reference-network.
Does not produce a candidate table or a messenger choice.
